scope: All /docs/ URLs in the retrieved sitemap, including all returned chunks. External links, screenshots, marketing pages and interactive generator behavior are not validated.
method: Read public documentation and inspect local handlers/services/tests. Original implementation only; command registration is NOT behavioral parity. No live Telegram tests, production migration or deployment.

features.differences_and_remaining: Navigation, setup and conventions reviewed. Settings syntax is not uniform across existing modules; no full parity claim.

Live authorization is intentional, not permission caching. Anonymous verification buttons are absent; personal-identity routes stay protected. Public lists now omit anonymous admins. Adminerror does not cover every independent plugin.
Atomic idempotent PostgreSQL approvals. Username/reason support and owner-confirmed bulk removal still need work. Exemptions cover existing automatic protections, not unimplemented ones.

Additional variants use durable intent/outcome records and command replay protection in configured PostgreSQL mode. Existing /mute remains temporary by default for compatibility; new /dmute and untimed /smute are permanent. Timed manual actions require at least 60 seconds to avoid very short Telegram durations becoming permanent. Existing base commands retain their current target parser and audit path. No live Telegram verification or automatic recovery of pending cases.

Process-local bounded counters, at-count trigger, 30-second minimum window and cleanup on/off differ from reference defaults. Distributed counters and /setfloodmode alias are pending; no silent automatic actions.

Metadata, membership and private role consent implemented. /fedreason and /fednotif expose stored owner-managed preferences; /quietfed exposes a stored current-chat-owner-managed preference. No-argument reads show current values. These commands explicitly disclose that ban enforcement and notification delivery are unavailable: storing a preference does not enable delivery or silence. NO cross-chat ban enforcement yet. Pending: fban/unfban/fedstat, subscriptions, import/export, logs, delivery/recovery and owner notifications. Existing info handlers require explicit ID; creation is not private-only. Ownership transfer needs consent and deletion needs explicit confirmation.

Canonical SQL settings/revisions and per-message action claims/outcomes; safe bounded non-backtracking bitset glob matcher supports word-aware accent/case/space normalization, quoted phrases, emoji and full filename globs via file:. Advanced selectors: prefix: anchors to the normalized message start (word-aware end), exact: anchors both ends, name: matches sender display name, username: matches the full sender username without @; all support the same bounded glob language. Group action modes nothing/warn/ban/mute/kick/tban/tmute, deletion toggle, default/per-trigger plain-text reasons, paginated native tables, read-only Group Management card and owner-confirmed clear. Limits: 100 triggers, 128 input characters per trigger, 500-character reasons, timed actions 60s–365d. Wildcard-only triggers refused. Parenthesized bulk add/remove accepts up to 20 triggers with quoted phrases and one shared reason, committed atomically as a single revision. Remaining: per-trigger action overrides, sticker/emoji packs, forwards, inline/lookalike selectors, typed-lock precedence and automated silent mode. Warn uses the existing legacy warning store/escalation; canonical warning authority remains pending. Other automatic protection watchers remain independent and can overlap. Legacy /antispam keyword policy is preserved separately; it is not silently converted into word-aware blocklists. No live Telegram validation.

Typed native-message deletion locks now run before blocklists, exempt Telegram admins, verify bot delete rights and use existing tenant/group ChatStore with confirmed PostgreSQL flush. Supports audio/contact/document/gif/location/photo/poll/sticker/video/videonote/voice/game/emojigame/album/inline/text; all means only this explicit set. Multi-type changes validate before mutation; failure restores prior cached policy. No schema migration. Remaining: other Rose types, entity/url/invite matching, warn/custom modes, reasons, allowlists, approved-user semantics, durable enforcement claim/audit tables and cross-process settings revision transactions. Existing optional antiflood watcher remains independent; this is not full Rose precedence across all protection systems. No live Telegram validation.
No raid-state authority, timed join bans or automatic join-rate detection.

Existing verification is not proof of documented captcha mode coverage. Review button/text/math/text2, join-request portals, durable challenge expiry, rules consent and restart recovery before claiming parity.

Existing moderator /note is member metadata, not named notes. Named notes, attachments, private/admin-only retrieval, hashtag triggers and recurring schedules remain absent. /clear collides with existing Music command ownership; do not silently replace it.

Atomic shared SQL state, plain-text replies, substring first-stored matching. Pending quoted/bulk triggers, media, prefix/exact patterns and fillings. /stop belongs to Music; retain /stopfilter rather than silently shadow it.
No private-to-group authorization bridge. Every connected read/write will need fresh membership/admin checks and isolated response routing; banned/left users must lose access.

Legacy warning state and thresholds still need canonical awaited relational persistence. Defaults differ intentionally (mute escalation). Missing timed modes, expiry, per-warning removal button and several documented command names.
Current pins retained. Permapin, unpinall alias, linked-channel anti-pin and cleanup options remain absent.
Existing bounded purge behavior retained; does not establish reference reply-range semantics. Missing /del, /spurge, /purgefrom and /purgeto.
Current report review workflow retained. Reference reports on/off, hidden admin tags, @admin watcher and staff-report rules need comparison; report storage is legacy document-backed.

Current /setlog and /log are deployment Owner diagnostics/log settings, NOT per-group reference category logs. Preserve identifiers and Owner isolation; use a deliberate routing design before adding group log controls.
Plugin activation gates are not per-chat user-command disable rules. Disabled/delete/admin override policies remain absent.
Shared SQL authority and immutable revisions. Missing private delivery/deeplink membership authorization and rule-button configuration; /setrules clear already removes published text.
Shared SQL greetings and controls exist. Media, richer fillings, setgoodbye/reset aliases, noformat preview and cleanup schedules need implementation/review; no equivalence claim.
Native Rich Message UI remains preferred. Reference message-template parser, safe buttonurl grammar, note menus, random variants and fillings are not implemented by UI table support.

Opt-in /cleanservice supports an explicit allowlist of joins, leaves, pins, title/photo changes and videochat notices. On selects these known categories only; off disables deletion. Selection replaces the previous list atomically with SQL revisions and per-tenant/group isolation. Requires a personal administrator with Delete messages; watcher rechecks bot deletion rights. Ordinary messages, payment/migration/topic events and unknown service types are untouched. Other join/leave watchers remain independent. Deleting a pin notice does not unpin it. Deletion failures are logged without raw exception content and not automatically retried; no durable deletion outcome history yet. /cleancommand all|on|off and /keepcommand all provide opt-in post-handler cleanup of recognized commands, including handled denials, using awaited per-group SQL settings/revisions. Applies to every supported prefix and checks bot deletion rights; private chats, unknown commands, other bots and handler exceptions are untouched. Unlike the reference, all currently means recognized commands only. Pending: admin/user/other command categories and unknown-command cleaning, category-aware bot-message cleanup, delayed deletion scheduling and remaining service categories. No live Telegram validation.
No general group import/export/reset. Requires bounded versioned parsers, creator-only import/reset confirmation and atomic authority-specific updates; never import credentials or ownership.

Create, rename, close and reopen forum topics using current Manage topics rights for caller and bot, with no bot-owner bypass. Current forum status is fetched live. Commands reject anonymous senders, ambiguous/missing thread IDs, invalid UTF-16 title length, and non-forum chats. General-topic thread ID 1 uses dedicated Telegram methods. False or exception API outcomes never claim success or auto-retry. No local duplicate settings scope: group settings remain shared. /actiontopic and /setactiontopic expose a tenant/group-scoped, transactionally audited destination for both welcome and goodbye messages. Defaults to General; setting General explicitly resets routing there. Destination changes require live Manage topics rights for caller/bot and a valid current thread. Greeting delivery reads the shared destination and never retries in another topic on failure or configured database outage. Pending: irreversible topic deletion with explicit confirmation, durable intent/outcome replay records and topic audit history. No live Telegram validation.
No complete translation catalog or per-group language selector. Do not advertise languages based only on Unicode support.
No private user-data inventory/export/erasure controls. Requires retention/legal and cross-store ownership review; do not delete moderation evidence indiscriminately.
Existing identity/member profile commands retained; connections and federation ban-status enrichment are absent.
Manual silent restriction variants are separate. Automated silent actions require per-chat owner consent, authorized log delivery and safe fallback when logs are unavailable.
No reviewed bot-to-bot command approval workflow. Do not introduce bot-triggered admin mutation bypasses or LLM-controlled shell execution.
No echo/say/broadcast equivalent added. Owner-only scoped broadcast would need explicit targeting, throttling, cancellation and audit; never reuse parent credentials for clones.
